name: Molina Healthcare

profile.address: 5610, Turing Road Southeast, Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, New Mexico, 87106
profile.reading:
This building in Albuquerque's Mesa del Sol district houses a data center that Molina Healthcare, a publicly traded managed-care and health-insurance company (NYSE: MOH), built through a separately registered subsidiary, Molina Healthcare Data Center, Inc. Molina announced the project in August 2008 as part of a plan to relocate and consolidate its data-processing operations from Long Beach, California to New Mexico, centralizing the technology that supports claims processing, member services, and health-plan administration across the subsidiary Medicaid and Medicare plans Molina then operated in sixteen states.

Public financing records from the New Mexico Finance Authority show the project drew on New Markets Tax Credit financing: an $8 million allocation closed in October 2011, structured with Wells Fargo Community Investment Holdings as the tax-credit investor and Molina, Inc. itself as the leverage lender, a financing pattern New Mexico has used on other projects to attract facilities that create technical jobs outside the state's traditional economic centers.

Construction records from ARCO National Construction, the general contractor, describe a roughly 26,500-square-foot building containing about 10,150 to 10,300 square feet of raised-floor computer-room space on 30-inch flooring, built out in three phases so the facility could stay operational throughout construction. The building achieved LEED Gold certification. Electrical-contractor records add further detail: the site takes primary utility service at 12.47 kilovolts through a customer-owned meter, distributes power through dual 5,000-amp main-tie-main generator paralleling switchgear, and backs up the load with roughly 4 megawatts of uninterruptible power supply capacity and about 10 megawatts of standby generation. Public project descriptions cite an initial IT capacity of about 6 megawatts with room to scale to roughly 12 megawatts as demand grows. The data-center portion of the project was substantially complete by fall 2011.

As with most enterprise data centers built by insurers, hospital systems, and banks, this facility exists to run Molina's own claims and member-services infrastructure rather than to lease space to outside tenants, so it does not appear in commercial colocation marketing. Beyond the original 2008 announcement and the 2011 construction and financing record, no more recent disclosure on current utilization, capacity upgrades since 2011, or any expansion has been made public by Molina.

reading:
Molina Healthcare, Inc. is a publicly traded managed care organisation listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker MOH and headquartered in Long Beach, California. It appears in this registry because of a single purpose built enterprise data centre in Albuquerque, New Mexico, held through a separately registered subsidiary called Molina Healthcare Data Center, Inc. Molina announced the project on 20 August 2008, describing a roughly 25,000 square foot building in Albuquerque's Mesa del Sol district that would house an IT centre of about 12,000 square feet, up from the 2,000 square feet the function then occupied, with operations beginning in 2009 and the building targeted at LEED Silver certification.

The finished building is better documented than the announcement. The general contractor of record describes a completed data centre of 26,170 square feet certified LEED Gold, with 10,300 square feet of 30 inch raised floor for underfloor cooling and cable management, a fully redundant electrical system fed at 12,470 volts primary, roughly 19,800 linear feet of underground duct bank, and a build carried out in three phases while the facility stayed live. That account gives an initial power capacity of six megawatts designed for later expansion to twelve. Those are electrical service figures tied to a medium voltage primary service, not a stated critical IT load. Molina publishes no IT load number for the site, and this registry does not convert one into the other.

The public finance record is more specific than earlier notes on this entry suggested. New Mexico Finance Authority material places Molina Healthcare Data Center, Inc. in the New Markets Tax Credit programme rather than under industrial revenue bonds, with an $8,000,000 Finance New Mexico allocation, a closing in October 2011, Wells Fargo Community Investment Holdings as the tax credit investor and Molina as leverage lender. That record describes a 26,500 square foot facility at Mesa del Sol, gives the purpose as consolidating the data requirements of Molina and the health plans it then ran in 16 states, cites reduced natural disaster exposure compared with California as part of the rationale, and notes that Molina already employed about 175 people in New Mexico.

The building itself is recorded at 5610 Turing Road SE in southeast Albuquerque, single storey, with a construction year of 2010. Nothing published establishes the current occupancy, utilisation or generator configuration, and Molina does not report facility level detail in its securities filings.
